news.title: Sprott Asset Management's Jacob White on uranium stocks sell-off and the case for a recovery
news.summary:
Sprott Asset Management Director of ETF Product Management Jacob White talked with Proactive's Stephen Gunnion about the sharp sell-off in uranium mining stocks, the disconnect with physical uranium prices and the potential catalysts for a recovery.

White explained that uranium equities have come under pressure despite spot prices rising more than 10% year to date to above US$90 per pound, while long-term contract prices have reached fresh highs.

He attributed the weakness largely to broader market volatility and pressure on risk assets rather than any deterioration in uranium fundamentals.

The interview also explores nuclear power's long-term growth prospects, with White highlighting energy security, reliable baseload electricity and rising demand from data centres as important drivers.

On the supply side, he pointed to a continuing uranium deficit, reduced production guidance from Cameco and tightening utility inventories.

White also discussed the prospect of increased utility contracting as buyers seek to secure future supplies, alongside new reactor construction, restarts and plant-life extensions.

He explained why improving market liquidity could help uranium mining shares reconnect with the strength of the physical market.
